column3: The Asherah image is singular in Hebrew. The naming of Nehushtan is expressed by an active singular verb.
The Hebrew says he “clung” to the LORD.
The Hebrew says “they captured it”, without explicitly naming the Assyrians.
The Hebrew says “I have sinned” and “I will bear” what is imposed.
The Hebrew says he cut off the doors and doorposts; gold is not explicitly named here.
The Hebrew repeats both going up and coming before describing where they stood.
The Hebrew calls these “a word of lips”.
The pierced part is specifically the palm.
Repelling is expressed as turning back an officer’s face.
The Hebrew names the language Judean and describes the hearing as the ears of the people.
Urine is called the “water of their feet”.
The Hebrew names the language Judean and uses both “spoke” and “said”.
The Hebrew says “his hand” rather than “my hand”.
